Bananas are berries, but strawberries are not.
Strawberries carry their seeds on the outside.
Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts.
Almonds, cashews and walnuts aren't true nuts in the botanical sense either.
Tomatoes are botanically fruits.
Cucumbers, pumpkins and peppers are botanically fruits too.
Rhubarb is a vegetable, though it's usually cooked like a fruit.
Pineapples take about two years to grow.
A pineapple is actually many fruits fused together.
Apples belong to the rose family.
Pears, plums, cherries and almonds are also in the rose family.
Avocados are single-seeded berries.
Coconuts are drupes, not true nuts.
Cashew nuts grow hanging below a fleshy 'cashew apple'.
Vanilla comes from the seed pods of an orchid.
Vanilla is one of the most labour-intensive spices because its flowers are often hand-pollinated.
Saffron comes from the stigmas of a crocus flower.
It takes well over 100,000 crocus flowers to make a kilogram of saffron.
Cinnamon is the inner bark of trees in the genus Cinnamomum.
Black pepper comes from dried berries of a climbing vine.
Coffee 'beans' are the seeds of a cherry-like fruit.
Chocolate comes from the seeds of the cacao tree.
Cacao pods grow directly on the trunk of the tree.
Black tea and green tea come from the same plant: Camellia sinensis.
Bamboo is a grass, and some species can grow almost a metre in a day.
Some bamboo species flower only once every several decades, all at the same time.
Sunflowers' seeds are arranged in spirals that follow Fibonacci numbers.
Young sunflowers turn to follow the sun across the sky.
Giant sequoias are the most massive single trees on Earth.
Coast redwoods are the tallest trees, over 115 m.
Hyperion, a coast redwood, is about 116 m tall.
Some bristlecone pines in California are more than 4,800 years old.
Pando, a grove of quaking aspens in Utah, is one connected organism.
Pando may be one of the heaviest living organisms on Earth.
The baobab tree can store thousands of litres of water in its trunk.
Oak trees can produce tens of thousands of acorns in a good year.
Ginkgo biloba is a 'living fossil' little changed for millions of years.
Ginkgo trees survived the atomic bombing of Hiroshima close to the blast.
The Wollemi pine was known only from fossils until it was found alive in 1994.
The corpse flower smells like rotting meat to attract pollinating flies.
Rafflesia arnoldii produces the largest single flower on Earth.
The titan arum has one of the largest flowering structures in the world.
Venus flytraps count touches before snapping shut.
Venus flytraps grow wild only in a small area of the Carolinas.
Pitcher plants trap insects in pools of digestive fluid.
Sundews catch insects with sticky droplets on their tentacles.
Mimosa pudica folds its leaves when touched.
Some plants release chemical signals when they're being eaten.
Trees can share nutrients through underground fungal networks.
Most plants form partnerships with fungi in their roots.
Mushrooms are more closely related to animals than to plants.
The largest known organism is a honey fungus in Oregon spreading over about 9 km².
Some mushrooms glow in the dark.
Lichens are partnerships between fungi and algae or cyanobacteria.
Moss can survive drying out completely and revive with water.
Ferns reproduce with spores rather than seeds.
Plants were on land long before the first dinosaurs.
Grasses cover a large share of Earth's land surface.
Wheat, rice and maize provide a large part of the calories eaten worldwide.
Rice is the staple food for more than half of the world's population.
Potatoes were first domesticated in the Andes of South America.
Tomatoes, maize, chocolate and chilli all originated in the Americas.
Potatoes and tomatoes are in the nightshade family.
Aubergines (eggplants) are also in the nightshade family.
Chilli peppers get their heat from capsaicin.
Birds can't feel the burn of capsaicin, so they happily spread chilli seeds.
Carrots were mostly purple or yellow before orange varieties became popular.
Broccoli, cabbage, kale and cauliflower were all bred from the same wild plant.
Garlic, onions and leeks are close relatives.
Peppermint is a natural hybrid of watermint and spearmint.
Basil is in the mint family.
Lavender is in the mint family too.
Cotton is mostly cellulose, the main structural material of plants.
Paper is usually made from wood pulp.
Cork is the bark of the cork oak, which regrows after harvesting.
Rubber comes from the latex sap of the rubber tree.
Maple syrup is made by boiling down maple sap.
It takes around 40 litres of maple sap to make one litre of syrup.
Tulips were once so valuable in the Netherlands that bulbs sold for extraordinary prices.
The Netherlands is the world's biggest exporter of flowers.
Roses have prickles, not true thorns.
Orchids are one of the largest flowering plant families, with over 25,000 species.
Some orchids trick insects by mimicking female bees.
Seeds of the sacred lotus have germinated after more than 1,000 years.
A date palm was grown from a roughly 2,000-year-old seed found at Masada.
Dandelion seeds can travel kilometres on the wind.
Coconuts can float across oceans and still sprout.
Plants make their food through photosynthesis using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide.
Leaves are green because chlorophyll reflects green light.
Autumn colours appear when chlorophyll breaks down and reveals other pigments.
Cacti store water in thick, fleshy stems.
Saguaro cacti may not grow their first arm until they're about 50–75 years old.
Welwitschia in the Namib Desert grows just two leaves for its whole life.
Some Welwitschia plants are thought to be over 1,000 years old.
Seagrass meadows store large amounts of carbon.
Kelp can grow up to around half a metre a day.
Kelp is a type of algae, not a true plant.
Phytoplankton produce around half of the oxygen made by photosynthesis on Earth.
The Amazon rainforest is home to around 16,000 tree species.
Tropical rainforests cover a small share of land but hold over half of land species.
